title: Tungsten Carbide

outline.arc: A resting carbide tip starts a question; a pen reveals its everyday use; a soap scratch and chalk/eraser comparison separate hard from tough; pole tips and a steel-backed tooth show how engineers choose materials.

beatIntents.intent: Introduce a resting carbide-tipped tooth on linen and the question of hard versus tough; no tool is operated or held.
Discover the rolling carbide ball in an ordinary pen; prose explains joining tungsten with carbon, pressing powder and heating, with a cobalt binder.
Big performs a gentle craft-stick scratch on soap over a tray; Little only predicts, watches and records.
Compare two already separated chalk pieces with Big gently bending an eraser; no flying pieces, powder cloud or child handling.
Follow the pair onto a calm snowy path, with pole tips planted into the ground; small carbide tips serve a specific job.
Return to the shared notebook and compare a hard carbide tip with the tougher steel body supporting it; leave a material-choice question open.
